subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: Conductors and Insulators: Why Copper but Not Rubber
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Conductors and Insulators: Why Copper but Not Rubber.

hook.text: Copper carries electricity. Rubber stops it. The difference is whether electrons can move freely.

buildup.text: In conductors, outer electrons aren't tightly bound to atoms. An electric field pushes them along like a river.

discovery.text: Insulators grip their electrons tightly. Even strong voltage can't pry them loose — until it can, and that's a spark.

twist.text: Semiconductors sit between the two. Silicon barely conducts on its own, but add impurities and it becomes controllable.

climax.text: Every computer chip is built from semiconductor junctions. The entire digital age depends on silicon's switchable conductivity.

punchline.text: Free electrons: conductor. Locked electrons: insulator. Switchable: revolution.

quiz.question: What makes semiconductors special compared to conductors and insulators?
options: They conduct only at high temperatures, acting as safety switches
Adding impurities makes their conductivity controllable and switchable
They are lighter than both conductors and insulators
